handfixes.summary: SYNOLOGY_TLS_FINGERPRINT pins and SYNOLOGY_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY skips TLS verification on the standard transport; no DSM request (probe, login, authenticated read or write, logout) follows a redirect, same origin included: every DSM http.Client's CheckRedirect is dsm.RefuseRedirect, a 3xx net/http returns unfollowed is an error too, the refusal names the status only and is not retried
handfixes.why: Most NAS units serve DSM's self-signed certificate. Only the h2-only browser-chrome transport emits --insecure, and that transport cannot reach DSM over plain HTTP or with HTTP/2 off (DSM's default). DSM's WebAPI never redirects; the generated client followed same-origin redirects on authenticated requests, so a NAS (or anything on the path) answering a read with 302 Location: /webapi/entry.cgi?api=SYNO.ActiveBackup.Task&method=backup&...&_sid=... made the client carry the sid and SynoToken into a backup start through the read-only abb_tasks tool, even with SYNOLOGY_MCP_READ_ONLY=1. handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: no credential-named field (password, passwd, secret, token, private key, API key, sid, did, ...) from a DSM answer reaches disk: rows are redacted at the single store sink (upsertGenericResourceTx, which sync, write-through live reads and the FTS index share), and an answer carrying one is never written to the HTTP response cache; live output is unchanged
handfixes.why: The spec declares no response schemas, so the secret-bearing reads cannot be enumerated; the class is reachable mechanically. Measured on the shipped binary against a stub NAS serving SENTINEL-SECRET-7731 in user passwd, share enc_passwd, Hyper Backup repo_password, ABB smtp_password and network pppoe_password: `sync` and the write-through of `hyperbackup tasks` stored it in data.db (which MCP sql serves even in read-only mode) and the response cache kept three copies. The fleet mirror stores typed columns only (first_error uses an allow-list of log params), so fleet sync never stored it. No synology GET is known or declared to return credential material, so no command moved to the Credential tier. TestSyncAndLiveReadsNeverPersistSecretFields walks the whole home after sync and live reads and fails with either sink's redaction removed; TestStoreNeverPersistsSecretFields and TestResponseCacheNeverStoresSecretFields pin each sink.

handfixes.summary: fleet add, fleet remove (registry administration) and tail are never MCP tools (mcp:hidden), in full and read-only mode; fleet_sync stays exposed and reaches only operator-registered NAS units

Measured on the shipped binaries: the attacker host received the password. tail defaults to --follow and polls forever, so an MCP tools/call never returned and hung an unattended agent (no result in 20 s). fleet_add/fleet_remove are hand-written (fleet_registry.go); tail.go is generated. TestMCPOmitsOperatorOnlyAndStreamingTools and TestMCPFleetSyncReachesOnlyRegisteredNAS fail with any of the three annotations removed.

handfixes.summary: a NAS certificate that does not match the pin is its own error kind (dsm.PinMismatchError / ErrCertificatePinMismatch): transport errors, fleet sync rows, live commands and doctor say 'the NAS certificate does not match the pinned SHA-256 fingerprint' with the presented fingerprint and the re-pin remedy, and the generated client does not retry it; the remedy is to verify the presented fingerprint in DSM and pin that value with --tls-fingerprint (or SYNOLOGY_TLS_FINGERPRINT), never a blind --pin-cert
handfixes.why: A pin mismatch read as 'the request failed (connection error or malformed response)', so a NAS that renewed its certificate (DSM self-signed renewal, Let's Encrypt every ~90 days) silently broke every sync; a live call over a cached session retried it three times with back-off (7 s) before failing. TestPinMismatchIsNamedEverywhere, TestPinMismatchIsItsOwnErrorKind and TestPinMismatchIsNotRetried fail with the description or the no-retry check removed.

handfixes.summary: sync (and workflow archive) store folder, group, package and user; the DSM system log (SYNO.Core.SyslogClient.Log) is not a sync resource and the log command reads it live only (no write-through, --data-source local refused)
handfixes.why: SyslogClient.Log items (time, level, descr, who, logtype) carry no id, so the log resource aborted as critical and `sync` exited 1 on every run against a real DSM shape (workflow archive too); the incomplete sync_state then made every MCP sql/search answer say the latest sync was incomplete, and the live log command printed a 'not cached locally' warning on every call. TestSyncSucceedsOnRealDSMShapes fails with log restored to the sync defaults, the workflow list or the log command's auto strategy.

handfixes.summary: every successful DSM answer (the generated client's success return and its response-cache read; the fleet dsm.Client.Get) passes dsm.MaskResponse with every secret VALUE the client holds (configured password, one-time code, trusted-device token, raw auth_header sid, every sid and SynoToken held), covering JSON-escaped, percent-encoded (once or twice), HTML-escaped and any decodable form; every non-empty secret is masked when it is an entire string value, whatever its length, and inside larger text from 8 characters on; masking is type-preserving: only string values change, never a number, boolean or null, and an object key is never renamed for a short secret; masked text reads [redacted]
handfixes.why: Credential-VALUE redaction covered only error text. If login returned sid SID-LEAK-7731 and a later answer carried that value in any field (a user's description, say), it reached stdout, the response cache, the local store and export. TestSecretValuesNeverLeaveTheClient (stdout, store, cache, export), TestCachedAnswersAreMaskedToo and TestFleetClientMasksSecretValues fail with the funnel removed. Round 3: a secret shorter than 4 characters (SYNOLOGY_PASSWORD=abc) as an entire field was never masked, and a number token equal to a held secret (a 6-digit one-time code equal to a result_id) was rewritten to the string "[redacted]", so the typed fleet parser failed fleet sync and abb triage with 'no valid result_id' while <prefix>_OTP_CODE was set. TestMaskingIsTypePreservingAndCoversShortSecrets, TestShortSecretsAndOneTimeCodesAreMaskedWherever and TestFleetSyncWithAOneTimeCodeEqualToAResultID fail with either rule reverted.

handfixes.summary: a session (sid, SynoToken, cookies, trusted-device token) is restored only for the exact origin and account it was saved for: newSessionManager loads nothing, ConfigureDSM empties and re-binds the cookie jar to the new origin and clears every session field before loading, loadFromDisk returns with no NAS address or no account and never reads the legacy origin-less session.json, the cached device token needs the record's exact origin and account; the jar (dsm.OriginJar) stores and returns cookies only for its one scheme://host:port and stores an https:// origin's cookies Secure
handfixes.why: newSessionManager called loadFromDisk before the origin was configured: an unexpired legacy session.json without an account passed the empty-account check, the origin check was skipped because the base URL was still empty, its cookies were restored without Secure, and ConfigureDSM cleared the sid but kept the jar, so a request to http://<same host> carried cookies saved for https://. TestLegacySessionNeverLoaded, TestReconfigureResetsTheSession and TestOriginJarBindsCookiesToOneOrigin fail with the binding reverted.

handfixes.summary: one canonical session key, dsm.SessionKey (= CanonicalAddress: lower-case scheme and host, default port written out, reverse-proxy path kept, no trailing slash), names the per-NAS session file (dsm.SessionFilePath), is the origin recorded in it (session manager and fleet SaveDeviceID), and every comparison against a recorded origin goes through dsm.SameSession (session reuse and the trusted-device token cache), in the generated session manager and the fleet client alike
handfixes.why: saveToDisk recorded the full SYNOLOGY_BASE_URL as the origin while loadFromDisk asked CachedDeviceIDFile for dsm.Origin(baseURL) (scheme://host only) and the file was named by scheme://host, so with a reverse-proxied address (https://proxy/nas1) or an upper-case scheme the exact-origin check never matched and every relogin after the session ended demanded a fresh one-time code; two NAS behind one proxy also shared one file. TestTrustedDeviceTokenBehindAProxyPath and TestSessionKeyIsOneCanonicalKey fail with the key reverted.

handfixes.summary: RegisterTools installs installRequiredArgsGuard, a server middleware that refuses every tools/call omitting (absent, null or blank) an argument the tool's own input schema marks required, before the handler runs: endpoint reads and writes, the Cobra mirror and novel tools alike; the result is an MCP error '<tool> requires "<arg>" (missing or empty); nothing was sent'
handfixes.why: mcp-go advertises a schema's required list but does not enforce it, and the generated endpoint handler forwards whatever it gets: abb_backup and abb_cancel declare task_ids as required, yet a call with no task_ids sent the backup/cancel write with no task list (the CLI refuses the same call). TestMCPRequiredArgsAreEnforced (through the server's own message path) fails with the guard removed.

handfixes.summary: a JSON flag that does not parse (--task-ids on abb backup/cancel, --additional on the promoted list commands) is a usage error, exit 2, as SKILL.md documents
handfixes.why: The generated commands return a plain error for an unparseable JSON flag, which isCobraUsageError did not recognise, so `abb backup --task-ids not-json` exited 1 (Codex round 4). One classifier rule covers every generated JSON flag. TestInvalidJSONFlagIsUsageError fails with the rule removed.

handfixes.summary: a positional a command needs is declared once, as "<name>" in Use (abb triage <task>, abb device <host-name>, fleet add/remove <name>), so the Cobra mirror's MCP schema requires it and the required-argument guard refuses a tool call without it; the CLI enforces the same declaration in one place (a hook wrapping the root PersistentPreRunE, before any other pre-run step): a call missing or blanking a required positional exits 2 naming it ('<path> requires <name> (missing or empty); nothing was run'), a bare call prints the help (exit 0), --dry-run does not waive it (only the press verify/dogfood harness does); and Cobra's own positional-count refusals (accepts N arg(s) / between / at most / requires at least) are usage errors, exit 2, in isCobraUsageError
handfixes.why: abb triage and abb device declared their needed positional optional ([task], [host-name]), so their MCP tools did not require it and a call without it returned the command's help text with isError false (round-5 review); across the CLI the same omission exited 0 (help for recall, learnings forget and search even with --json; a dry-run plan for abb triage/device, learnings confirm/reject and fleet add/remove) or 1 (export, profile, client: Cobra's ExactArgs/RangeArgs message was not a recognised usage error). TestMissingRequiredPositionalIsRefused (every command in the tree, through the real Execute), TestRequiredPositionalsReadUseLikeTheMCPSchema and TestMirroredPositionalsAreRequired (every mirrored tool, through the server's message path) fail with the declarations, the hook or the classifier rule reverted.
